title: Intel CEO says Intel can serve only 50% of customers, attributes to CPU demand
gist: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan says CPU demand lets Intel supply only about 50% of customers, tying it to inference and agentic AI, and cites substrates and packaging as binding constraints and 95% reliance on one Taiwan-based foundry as dangerous. Q2 revenue rose 25% to $16.1B and shares are up about 175% YTD but 24% below their June high.

insights.claim: Intel can currently supply only about 50% of customer CPU demand, and many CEOs are calling the Intel CEO to apologize for not being able to produce enough.
insights.speaker: Lip-Bu Tan
insights.so_what: Supply-limited CPU market implies pricing power and revenue upside for Intel, plus signals for the wider server CPU supply chain.
insights.quote: CPU demand is so high that we can only supply 50% of customers
insights.locator: Intel CEO says Intel can serve only 50%

insights.claim: Intel's Q2 revenue rose 25% year over year to $16.1 billion, its strongest growth in 15 years, with demand outpacing growing supply.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Confirms an inflection in Intel's core product business after years of stagnation.

insights.claim: Tan argues AI is moving beyond GPU-driven training into inference and agent-based systems, creating demand for general-purpose CPUs as millions or trillions of agents will require compute and security.
insights.speaker: Lip-Bu Tan
insights.so_what: If agentic AI is CPU-intensive, the AI-capex beneficiaries broaden beyond GPUs to CPUs and servers.
insights.quote: in the future millions or trillions of agents will require resources

insights.claim: Tan says staying in manufacturing and advanced packaging is essential because computing is shifting to a system approach integrating CPU, memory and I/O.
insights.speaker: Lip-Bu Tan
insights.so_what: Packaging capability, not just wafer capacity, is a strategic moat and a rationale for Intel Foundry.
insights.quote: Everything is increasingly changing to a system approach and packaging, and this is the future.
insights.locator: Advanced packaging is becoming just as important

insights.claim: Substrates are one of Intel's biggest constraints, as Japanese and Taiwanese companies are securing sufficient quantities through prepayment.
insights.speaker: Lip-Bu Tan
insights.so_what: Substrate suppliers hold leverage; prepayment tactics tighten supply for latecomers, so watch substrate vendors' capacity and pricing.
insights.quote: Japanese and Taiwanese companies are securing sufficient quantities through prepayment

insights.claim: Tan calls relying 95% on one company, especially one based in Taiwan, very dangerous, framing Intel's foundry as geopolitical diversification.
insights.speaker: Lip-Bu Tan
insights.so_what: Supports the case for Western foundry customers and policy backing of Intel Foundry.
insights.quote: relying 95% on one company, especially one based in Taiwan, is very dangerous
insights.locator: Tan also framed Intel's foundry ambitions

insights.claim: Intel is proceeding with high-volume 14A production in 2028 after securing stronger customer demand, and its foundry business reported Q2 revenue of $5.77 billion.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: External customer demand for 14A de-risks the foundry capex story.

insights.claim: Manufacturing requires careful management of yields, defects, cycle times and variability, demands substantial capex, and the situation has improved over the past 18 months.
insights.speaker: Lip-Bu Tan
insights.so_what: Execution and capex intensity remain the key risks for Intel's turnaround.

insights.claim: Intel cut vice presidents from about 450 at peak to roughly 200 and management layers from 12 to six to speed decisions.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Organizational simplification is a leading indicator of execution improvement.
insights.locator: At the same time, Intel has been restructuring

insights.claim: Intel's market capitalization is about $574 billion with shares up roughly 175% year to date, closing at $108.60 and about 24% below the $142.35 52-week high from June 30.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Much of the turnaround is priced in, with the stock well off its high, so valuation depends on sustained supply expansion.
insights.locator: Intel currently has a market capitalization
